questions.q: What does "Start and wait for an approval" do that "Create an approval" alone does not?
options: It supports more approvers
It starts the request and pauses the flow until a response arrives, in one step
It skips the need for a Dataverse database
It only works with SharePoint as the data source
questions.explain: "Create an approval" starts the request and moves on immediately; pausing for the response requires a separate "Wait for an approval" step. "Start and wait for an approval" combines both into one action.

questions.q: Castlebridge Logistics needs both its operations manager and finance lead to sign off on a large freight claim before the flow continues. Which approval type fits?
options: Approve/Reject – First to respond
Approve/Reject – Everyone must approve
Custom Responses – Wait for one response
Sequential approval only if there are more than five approvers
questions.explain: "Everyone must approve" requires a response from every named approver before the flow continues, and a single rejection ends it — exactly the dual sign-off Castlebridge Logistics needs.

questions.q: In sequential approval, what determines when the next approver is asked to respond?
options: All approvers are asked at the same time
The previous approver in the defined order must respond first
A fixed 24-hour timer between each approver
Sequential approval has no defined order — it's random
questions.explain: Sequential approval requests approvers one at a time, in a specific order, and each approver must respond before the request moves to the next one.

questions.q: After "Start and wait for an approval" completes, how does a flow typically branch on whether it was approved or rejected?
options: It cannot branch — the flow always continues the same way
A Condition step checks the action's outcome output
By creating a second, identical approval action
By manually polling a SharePoint list
questions.explain: The approval action's output includes an outcome field with the approver's decision. A Condition step reads that field to split the flow into approved and rejected branches.

questions.q: What happens the first time anyone in a non-default Power Automate environment uses the approvals connector?
options: Nothing — approvals work identically everywhere with no setup
A Dataverse database is auto-provisioned, and the user running that first flow needs an administrator role in that environment
The flow fails permanently and must be rebuilt
A premium license is immediately required
questions.explain: Approval flows save their data in Dataverse. In a non-default environment, the database provisions automatically on first use, but the user triggering that first run needs an administrator role there.
